title: Charging for the Period a Keyturn Host Protection Plan Enrolment Went Without Cover
content:
The period an enrolment on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan went without cover is itself charged for, and what is charged for it is added last to the charge for restoring the cover. How the period is measured turns on whether a claim has been accepted on the enrolment.

- Where the enrolment went without cover for thirty days or more and no claim has been accepted on it in the twelve months before, the period without cover is measured in whole months of thirty days and each month is charged at a tenth of the plan's reinstatement fee, that is at 10 percent of it.
- Where the enrolment went without cover for thirty days or more and a claim has been accepted on it in that period, the period is measured in whole weeks of seven days and each week is charged at a fortieth of that fee, that is at 2.5 percent of it.
- Where the enrolment went without cover for fewer than thirty days, no charge is made for the period.

### Worked readings (hypothetical figures, on a published fee of 100)

| Days without cover | Claim accepted in the twelve months before | Charged for the period |
|---|---|---|
| 29 | either | nothing |
| 65 | no | 20.00, being 2 whole months of thirty days |
| 65 | yes | 22.50, being 9 whole weeks of seven days |
| 30 | no | 10.00, being 1 whole month of thirty days |

Part months and part weeks are not charged for: at 65 days the count is 2 whole months of thirty days or 9 whole weeks of seven days, and the remainder falls away. A period of exactly 30 days is thirty days or more, and a period of 29 days is not.

### Records consulted

The days without cover run from the day cover fell away on the enrolment, and the claims counted are the appraisals accepted on this enrolment within the twelve months before.
